questions: Does 'subsequence' mean any subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) as usual, and we are to find the maximum possible length among all such subsequences, or just the length of some arbitrary valid subsequence?

When the guarantee says X_i >= min of first R_i elements, does it imply there is always at least one element <= X_i in that prefix, but could the subsequence be empty if no element is <= X_i? (But guarantee ensures at least one element <= X_i, so subsequence length at least 1?)
Is the subsequence required to be strictly increasing by value, or strictly increasing by index? (Typically strictly increasing values, but could be ambiguous.)

For elements equal to X_i, are they allowed? The problem says 'at most X_i', so <= X_i, but strict increase means values must be strictly increasing; if two elements equal X_i, they cannot both be in subsequence.
Should the subsequence be chosen from the prefix up to R_i inclusive, meaning indices 1..R_i, or up to but not including R_i? (Given 'A_1, A_2, ..., A_{R_i}', it's inclusive.)

If multiple subsequences satisfy conditions, do we output the maximum length? (Implied by 'Find the length of such a subsequence' without 'longest', but typical competitive programming expects maximum.)
Are we allowed to reorder elements? Subsequence maintains original order, so no reordering.
Is the subsequence required to consist of elements whose values are at most X_i, but also must the subsequence itself be strictly increasing? That is clear from text.
